title: Naugatuck
summary: A mixed-use building on the Naugatuck River: four storeys of affordable apartments over retail, with a plaza and amphitheater lawn. WRT Planning + Design for Pennrose.
location: Maple Street & Old Firehouse Road, Naugatuck, CT
program: Affordable housing, retail, plazas and open space
body: Parcel B, Phase 1 of a mixed-use development on the Naugatuck River, designed at WRT Planning + Design for Pennrose. The building bends around the corner of Maple Street and Old Firehouse Road, holding both street edges, with retail and the residential lobby at grade and four storeys of apartments above.

The elevations are built from three families of cladding: a red running-bond brick that anchors the corner, a linen-colored stacked-bond brick along the long west face, and fiber-cement lap siding blended from three greys so the wall reads as texture rather than panel. A charcoal fiber-cement volume caps the north end, and a stained poplar veneer marks the entrances.

Apartments come in one- and two-bedroom types, each drawn in a Type A and a Type B variant — the first meeting ICC A117.1 and UFAS adaptable requirements, the second the visitable standard — so accessibility is distributed through the building rather than concentrated in a few units. The kitchens and bathrooms were drawn as a standard kit and repeated across the types.
